# ↪️ Pull Request

This pull request stops error messages from being shown when a server is interrupted with Ctrl-C. It fixes #5030.

The problem was introduced in #4971. Before that PR the call to `exit()` on line 247 had no argument, now the argument is `1` which causes `npm` & `yarn` to show an error.

## 🚨 Test instructions

You can test this with the examples in this repo. Before:
```
> yarn parcel server packages/examples/simple/index.html
yarn run v1.22.4
$ /workspaces/parcel/node_modules/.bin/parcel server packages/examples/simple/index.html
[press ctrl c here]
error Command failed with exit code 1.
info Visit https://yarnpkg.com/en/docs/cli/run for documentation about this command.

> echo $?
1
```

After:
```
> yarn parcel server packages/examples/simple/index.html
yarn run v1.22.4
$ /workspaces/parcel/node_modules/.bin/parcel server packages/examples/simple/index.html
[press ctrl c here]
Done in 29.55s.
> echo $?
0
```

## ✔️ PR Todo

- [ ] Added/updated unit tests for this change
- [x] Filled out test instructions (In case there aren't any unit tests)
- [x] Included links to related issues/PRs

issue_context.title: [Parcel2] Stopping parcel serve results in an error
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

Stopping `parcel serve` (with Ctrl+C on Windows) logs an error.

## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command)

Not relevant

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

Should silently stop serving parcel

## 😯 Current Behavior

Instead it stops serving parcel but at the same time it logs an error

```js
npm ERR! code ELIFECYCLE
npm ERR! errno 1
npm ERR! morpho@0.1.0 app2:start: `parcel serve webapp/src/app2/index.html --dist-dir webapp/dist/app2 -p 1002`
npm ERR! Exit status 1
npm ERR!
npm ERR! Failed at the morpho@0.1.0 app2:start script.
npm ERR! This is probably not a problem with npm. There is likely additional logging output above.

npm ERR! A complete log of this run can be found in:
npm ERR!     C:\Users\MeMe\AppData\Roaming\npm-cache\_logs\2020-08-17T13_19_28_609Z-debug.log
```

## 💁 Possible Solution

Handle the error

## 🔦 Context

Not relevant

## 💻 Code Sample

Not relevant

## 🌍 Your Environment

<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           | 2.0.0-nightly.368
| Node             | v14.5.0
| npm/Yarn         | 6.14.5
| Operating System | Windows 10
comments:
I have narrowed down the nightly build that introduced the bug.
Last build stopping `parcel serve` without error was:
`2.0.0-nightly.357`
The first where the error has been introduced:
`2.0.0-nightly.358`
Possibly:  #4971
I'm seeing this on linux too. I just created PR #5128 which I think should fix it.
I believe this was fixed by #5130

review_comments:
This seems to run this way no matter how Parcel was invoked (`serve`, `build`, etc.). I don't think it's a good idea to exit with a successful exit code when interrupting Parcel when used with `build` (could be a production build). 

Can we retain the non-zero code when interrupting `parcel build`?
